items.stem: OPC UA is widely used in IIoT because it provides:

options.text: A secure, vendor-neutral standard for industrial machine-to-machine data exchange
options.rationale: Correct: OPC UA offers interoperable, secure industrial communication.
OPC UA is a communication standard, not a file format.

options.text: A brand of programmable logic controller
options.rationale: OPC UA is a protocol, not a PLC brand.

options.text: A type of physical network cable
options.rationale: OPC UA is a protocol layer, not cabling.

items.explanation: Correct: OPC UA offers interoperable, secure industrial communication.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound practices when connecting OT to IT? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Segment networks so operational technology is isolated and controlled
options.rationale: Correct: segmentation limits the spread of threats into OT.

options.text: Apply security monitoring across the OT/IT boundary
options.rationale: Correct: monitoring the boundary detects intrusions early.

options.text: Give every machine a direct public internet connection
options.rationale: Direct public exposure is a serious OT risk.

options.text: Use shared default passwords across all devices
options.rationale: Shared defaults are an easily exploited weakness.

items.explanation: Correct: segmentation limits the spread of threats into OT.

items.stem: A digital twin is best described as:

options.text: A live virtual model of a physical asset, updated with its real data
options.rationale: Correct: a digital twin mirrors the real asset using its sensor data.

options.text: A backup copy of the machine's manual
options.rationale: A manual copy is not a digital twin.
A physical duplicate is not a digital twin.

options.text: A one-time CAD drawing never updated
options.rationale: A twin is continuously updated, unlike a static drawing.

items.explanation: Correct: a digital twin mirrors the real asset using its sensor data.
